Class GraphPicture

java.lang.Object
java.awt.Component
java.awt.Container
javax.swing.JComponent
org.aetheris.lcarsgraph.GraphPicture
All Implemented Interfaces:
ImageObserver, MenuContainer, Serializable
public final class GraphPicture extends JComponent
The picture paints one graph back to front. Hints do not move a coordinate.

  • Method Details

    • follow

      private void follow(String id, int ddx, int ddy)
      The method moves one dragged node with the pointer. The move stays on the event thread. A second thread would put the pointer behind a hop. The picture thread places a generation. It does not drag.
      Parameters:
      id - The id is the dragged node.
      ddx - The ddx is the pointer move in viewport pixels.
      ddy - The ddy is the pointer move in viewport pixels.

    • reveal

      private void reveal(String id)
      The method keeps the dragged node inside the viewport. A move that crosses the edge scrolls that axis. A margin that grows keeps the same screen seat.
      Parameters:
      id - The id is the dragged node.

    • panView

      private void panView(int ddx, int ddy)

    • armCoast

      private void armCoast(int physicalX, int physicalY)

    • coastStep

      private void coastStep()

    • stopCoast

      private void stopCoast()

    • home

      void home()
      The method returns the picture to the origin. A reset uses this seat.

    • holdFrame

      void holdFrame()
      The method remembers the zoomed-out frame. A later double-click keeps this frame.

    • frameFocus

      void frameFocus()
      The method seats the closer picture on the focused intent. The zoom moves to 200 when the open zoom is smaller. A showing viewport puts that intent at the center.

    • restoreFrame

      void restoreFrame()
      The method returns the zoomed-out frame.

    • dropFrame

      void dropFrame()
      The method forgets a held frame. A reset lays the picture out from the origin.

    • dropCluster

      void dropCluster()
      The method forgets the close ring. The next closer picture seats the doors again.
